cells.tense: You are reading the pattern in front of you and it is steering the next move.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have noticed but not yet put on the table, and say it out loud this week.
cells.core:
There is a shape in view that other people are still squinting at, and it is doing work on the road you are traveling. The heading is not held by force. You look at what is actually there, the pattern shows itself, and the next move follows it — which is why you keep moving when the road gets rough.

What ties this up is the same reading arrived at with someone else. What you find becomes a place for two people, not a verdict you carry alone. Spot the shape, then bring it to the person who can work it out with you. When something is read together, it stops being only yours to carry.

cells.tense: You are working out in advance how it will all read, long before there is anything on the road to read.
cells.ask: Take one plan and walk it today, on the steps already in front of you, all the way to a finished task.
cells.core:
You are diagramming the whole route before the first step is taken, and the diagramming has quietly become the goal. Somewhere ahead is the version where it all makes sense, and you are living there — the details checked and rechecked, the flaw caught before it arrives, the next step worked out before you have taken the one you are standing on.

Your reading is sharp, and right now it is running ahead of the road. What you work out keeps getting tested instead of traveled. Use it the way it was built to be used: take what is already under your feet and finish one small thing with it. The route was never the destination.

cells.tense: You can see the shape in front of you and you are not putting it into words.
cells.ask: Say the pattern out loud to one person before it is finished or polished, and leave it at that.
cells.core:
You can still make out what is going on better than most people around you. What stopped is saying it. The read stays with you while the road goes on without it — you spot the shape, you keep it, and the next step you take does not have it in it.

It is not the spotting that went quiet. It is the handoff. Someone else is standing on the road beside you, headed the same way, who could take what you find and put it to use. Hand one read over today. Nothing rides on it being right, and said badly is fine.

cells.tense: You are already steering by what you notice, and you keep calling it just how the work goes.
cells.ask: Write down one judgment you made in the last day that you did not say out loud in the moment.
cells.core:
The read comes fast and it holds. You walk into a room, take it in, and what is going on is clear to you before anyone has said much — right often enough that people lean on it without either of you naming it. That is the thing working, and it is why the heading stays.

What slips is the credit. You size things up and move, and you tell it like the situation sized itself up and you were just along for the ride. What got skipped is the simpler thing underneath: what you actually feel about what is in front of you. Before the analysis there is a pull, toward this and away from that, and the read stands on that pull. Let one of them stay yours instead of rounding it off into an assessment.
